names.name: Dunkin'
names.said: Dropped Donuts from the name in 2019 and kept the donuts.

text.what: The Quincy, Massachusetts chain that paired coffee and donuts nationally, and the oldest surviving company using the short spelling.
text.story: Bill Rosenberg opened the Open Kettle in 1948 and renamed it Dunkin' Donuts in May 1950. Franchising started in 1955. Allied Lyons, Baskin-Robbins' holding company, acquired the chain in 1990; its purchase of Mister Donut — founded by Rosenberg's former partner Harry Winokur — and the conversion of those shops drove North American growth the same year. Dawn Donuts went the same way.
text.today: New England independents compete on frying on site, which is the difference the chain's scale cannot copy shop by shop.
